A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IMPACT study. Their complete main texts and Appendices A-I, including equations, six tables and fifteen figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, robustness tests and other empirical analyses in Section 4 and Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including dataset comparisons, seen-versus-unseen evaluations and point-level detection results.

M1.justification: TIS, RADG, influence-guided label flipping, feature perturbation, dual learning heads, losses and inference scores are unchanged. Algorithm 1 is identical; the expanded problem statement introduces no new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UCR, ASD, PSM, SMD, CT, SAD, PTBXL and TUSZ, plus the same synthetic scalability scenarios. General and hard open-set settings and point-level task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including the seven unsupervised and seven open-set baselines, the seen-versus-unseen comparisons, and COE, WMix, COE-WMix and CAP augmentation comparisons. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sampling protocols, default 2% contamination, 20% validation split, training budgets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 4.1 and Appendices E-H. The new contamination clarification in Section 3 does not report a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: Table 3 ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity, contamination robustness, generation analyses, channel studies and visual case studies are retained unchanged. The new rare-subpopulation limitation is discussion, without an accompanying experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs and retain the same mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty procedures or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: The corresponding numerical entries, plotted results and empirical findings are unchanged. For example, IMPACT retains TUSZ AUC of 82.91 ± 0.74 in Table 1 and UCR VUS-ROC of 64.53 ± 0.01 in Table 6.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds a formal unseen-class definition, but prints U = S \ C despite S being a subset of C; the described remaining classes require C \ S. This introduces a localized mathematical error. The theorem statements, derivations and proofs in Appendices A-D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about influence-based decontamination, realistic pseudo-anomaly generation, robustness and detection of unseen anomalies. No core contribution is added or redefined.

C2.justification: Appendix I newly acknowledges that rare normal subpopulations without semantic overlap may be misclassified as anomalies, and suggests subpopulation discovery or group-aware validation. Section 3 also explicitly clarifies that unlabeled contamination may come from seen or unseen anomaly classes.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit IMPACT code-availability statement and repository address to the abstract, absent from v1. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information and baseline code sources remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Xu et al. (2023) and Zhang et al. (2026), and removes Sun et al. (2025), while retaining the central research positioning. CT and SAD source references become footnotes linking the same datasets rather than disappearing.

P1.justification: v2 condenses two related-work discussions, expands the problem statement, makes small language corrections, adds acknowledgements and updates the publication footer. The overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their content, but placement and surrounding text flow change. Figure 3 moves from the right to the left column on page 9, and Table 4 moves earlier within Appendix E. Other changes are limited layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added code-access information and concrete rare-subpopulation limitation modestly improve reproducibility documentation and transparency. These benefits outweigh the localized reversed set-difference error in Section 3, although that error weakens formal precision. The method, experimental evidence and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.
